articles.title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $100M+ homes, millions in charitable donations, foundation finances and multimillion-dollar business deals reveal the bigger story behind their growing fortune
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce have built lives that stretch far beyond music charts and football stadiums.
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce have built lives that stretch far beyond music charts and football stadiums. Their wealth now reaches into luxury real estate, charitable giving, brand partnerships and business investments. Swift's property portfolio has been estimated at more than $100 million, while Kelce continues to expand his interests beyond the NFL. Their charitable work has also attracted attention, from millions donated to food banks and children's organisations to Kelce's youth-focused foundation. Together, these developments offer a closer look at how the celebrity couple manages money, supports communities and builds financial influence beyond their careers.Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's luxury homes reflect their growing wealthReal estate is one of the clearest signs of the couple's financial success. Taylor Swift has spent years building a property portfolio across several major American cities, while Travis Kelce has invested in homes close to his football career and childhood roots.According to Business Insider, Swift's real estate holdings have been estimated at more than $100 million. Her properties include a waterfront mansion in Watch Hill, Rhode Island, a historic Beverly Hills estate and several homes in New York City. She also owns residences in Nashville, where her career began to take shape.Her Rhode Island property, purchased for $17.75 million in 2013, is among her best-known homes. The estate has become closely associated with her private summer gatherings. Her New York holdings include a Tribeca duplex and a neighbouring townhouse, giving her a substantial presence in one of the country's most expensive property markets.Kelce has also invested heavily in real estate. He bought a Leawood, Kansas, mansion for about $6 million in 2023. In March 2026, he purchased a historic lakefront estate in Bratenahl, Ohio, for $5.35 million.As reported by The Wall Street Journal, the Ohio property spans approximately 3.5 acres and features a 21,000-square-foot residence, eight bedrooms, a swimming pool and a guest cottage. The purchase added another major asset to Kelce's property holdings.However, the estate has attracted attention beyond its price. Plans to improve privacy at the property have faced objections from neighbours, including concerns about fencing, landscaping and local infrastructure. The dispute shows that even a luxury home can bring practical challenges.Millions in charitable donations go beyond one announcementThe couple's philanthropy deserves attention beyond any single headline. Taylor Swift has supported food banks, disaster relief efforts, education and other causes throughout her career.In October 2024, she donated $5 million to Feeding America following Hurricanes Helene and Milton. The money supported relief efforts for communities affected by the storms. In December 2025, she gave another $1 million to Feeding America and $1 million to the American Heart Association, with both organisations publicly acknowledging the gifts.Travis Kelce has focused much of his charitable work on children and underserved communities. Through his Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation, he has supported programmes designed to help young people develop skills, gain opportunities and build confidence.His work with Operation Breakthrough in Kansas City has been particularly notable. The organisation provides educational and support services for children and families. The Kansas City Chiefs reported in January 2026 that Kelce had contributed nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough over the years through personal donations and directed funds.Kelce has also used his NFL performance to encourage charitable giving. In a 2017 campaign, he pledged to match fan contributions up to $50,000 to support an after-school programme.The couple's largest reported joint charitable announcement came in July 2026, when they donated $26 million across 20 charities. According to the Associated Press, the recipients included food banks, children's hospitals, education programmes and animal welfare organisations.The individual amounts given to each organisation were not disclosed. Even so, the announcement highlighted the range of causes the couple supports, including organisations in communities that have played important roles in their lives.Travis Kelce's foundation finances face closer examinationCharitable giving has also brought questions about transparency. Travis Kelce's Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation has faced scrutiny over how its money was allocated in recent years.An investigation by The Arizona Republic, discussed in subsequent reporting, examined federal tax filings covering 2021 to 2024. Reports said the foundation recorded roughly $1.5 million in revenue and about $1.1 million in expenses over the period. One report cited approximately $446,000 in charitable spending and $469,000 in management costs.These figures have prompted questions about how much money reached charitable programmes compared with the costs of running the organisation. They do not, by themselves, establish wrongdoing. Nonprofit expenses can include staff, administration and programme support, and a fair assessment requires the full filings and a clear understanding of how spending was classified.Kelce's documented community work remains relevant to that discussion. His support for Operation Breakthrough and youth development programmes provides examples of the causes associated with his charitable efforts.For readers, the key distinction is between questioning financial reporting and assuming misconduct. A careful assessment should consider both the foundation's reported spending and the work it has carried out.Multimillion-dollar deals expand Kelce's business interestsTravis Kelce's earnings are no longer tied solely to his NFL contract and endorsement appearances. He has moved into investments and media, creating additional sources of commercial opportunity.One of his most prominent ventures is New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Jason Kelce. In 2024, the brothers signed a deal with Amazon-owned Wondery covering distribution and advertising rights. The agreement was widely reported to be worth more than $100 million over three years, although the precise financial terms were not officially disclosed.The figure belongs to the brothers' podcast agreement, not to Travis alone. Still, the deal demonstrates how their popularity has developed into a valuable media business.Kelce also became an investor and strategic partner in Sleep Number in January 2026. The company's regulatory filing confirmed a three-year partnership involving national advertising and stock compensation. His ownership stake was set to remain below 5%, and the exact value of the investment was not disclosed.Another development arrived in October 2026, when Garage Beer, the company Kelce co-owns with Jason and Andy Sauer, secured a $20 million revolving credit facility. The financing gives the business access to funds under agreed lending terms. It is not a $20 million personal payment to the brothers.These ventures show how Kelce is using his public profile to build commercial interests that can extend beyond his playing career.What their growing fortune really tells usTaylor Swift and Travis Kelce's financial lives combine personal assets, philanthropy and business interests, but the numbers should not be added together without care. A property's purchase price differs from its current market value. A corporate credit line is not personal income, and a reported podcast contract does not reveal each host's individual earnings.The same caution applies to charitable giving. Swift's individual donations, Kelce's foundation work and the couple's joint contributions represent different forms of support and should not be counted twice.What emerges is a broader picture of two high-profile figures using their success in different ways. Swift has built a substantial property portfolio alongside her music career and longstanding charitable work. Kelce has expanded from professional football into media, brand partnerships and private business investments, while maintaining a public commitment to youth-focused causes.Their growing fortune is therefore about more than luxury homes or headline-making deals. It also raises questions about how celebrity wealth is invested, how charitable organisations report their spending and how public influence can translate into lasting business and community impact.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: U2 to Headline Halftime Show of NFL Thanksgiving Eve Game Between Packers, Rams on Netflix
articles.summary: When the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams meet in a Thanksgiving Eve game on Nov. 25, fans will be treated to a halftime show involving one of the most iconic rock bands of all time.
articles.body:
When the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams meet in a Thanksgiving Eve game on Nov. 25, fans will be treated to a halftime show involving one of the most iconic rock bands of all time.

Netflix, which is the exclusive home of the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, announced Tuesday that U2 will perform during halftime at the Rams' SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California:

The Irish band, piloted by lead vocalist Bono, has won 22 Grammy Awards, and performed during halftime of Super Bowl XXXVI back in February 2002.

That Super Bowl halftime ranks among the most memorable and emotional of all time since it took place just months after the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

Bono famously revealed an American flag upon opening his jacket, and the New England Patriots went on to upset the then-St. Louis Rams in what was quarterback Tom Brady's first of seven Super Bowl wins.

When the Packers and Rams clash on Thanksgiving Eve, though, it could prove to be a massive game in terms of playoff positioning in the NFC.

If the regular season ended today, the Packers would be the No. 5 seed in the NFC with a 4-2 record, while the Rams would miss the postseason with a 2-4 mark.

The Rams' struggles thus far have been shocking given that they were the Super Bowl favorite after a busy offseason that saw them acquire cornerback Trent McDuffie and pass-rusher Myles Garrett in trades with the Kansas City Chiefs and Cleveland Browns, respectively.

Garrett has not played since Week 1 due to a knee injury, though, and star wide receiver Puka Nacua missed a pair of contests as well.

While losses to contending teams such as the San Francisco 49ers, Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills can be excused to some degree, Sunday's 18-16 home loss to the Arizona Cardinals came as a shock and suggests that head coach Sean McVay might have to make some changes.

As for the Packers, they have reeled off three consecutive wins after a 1-2 start, and they haven't even gotten their star defensive player back yet in pass-rusher Micah Parsons, who is working his way back from a torn ACL suffered last season.

Both Garrett and Parsons could potentially be back in the lineup when the Packers and Rams play on Thanksgiving Eve, adding some defensive firepower to two of the NFC's true heavyweights.

articles.title: Terry McLaurin injury update: Commanders veteran suffers brutal knee injury after a slight push from 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir
articles.summary: Washington Commanders veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin was carted off in the first quarter of the Week 6 game against the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body: Washington Commanders veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin was carted off in the first quarter of the Week 6 game against the San Francisco 49ers.As per head coach Dan Quinn, McLaurin may have suffered a significant season-ending injury. He will undergo MRI and further testing on Tuesday. “The concern is that it could be significant. We’ll do scans tomorrow and give you an update when I visit with you guys,” Quinn said.As a five-time 1,000-yard wide receiver, McLaurin’s presence is crucial to Washington’s offense - even with Stefon Diggs on the team. While Diggs missed Week 5 against the New York Giants due to a hamstring injury, he returned for Week 6.With Jayden Daniels returning from a major injury, Washington is incomplete without McLaurin’s veteran presence.What happened to Terry McLaurin?Washington Commanders wideout Terry McLaurin was running a route on a third-and-9 play in the first quarter of Monday’s 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers when 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, who was tightly covering him, slightly pushed him towards the sideline.With that slight push, McLaurin fell directly and awkwardly onto his knee. He toppled and grabbed his hurt left knee very tightly. Players from both teams came over to check on McLaurin.Washington’s medical staff came onto the gridiron. They placed his leg in a splint. He hobbled into the cart on his own. The medical staff carted him off in the first half of the Commanders vs. 49ers game.According to NFL Network’s Grant Gordon, even though McLaurin and Lenoir were engaged, it will be ruled a non-contact injury. Because his leg/knee was not contacted before he fell onto the gridiron.According to ProFootballDoc Dr. David J. Chao, McLaurin could have suffered a left patellar tendon rupture. “Leg just gives out. Horrible,” Chao wrote. The Washington WR may need surgery and could miss the 2026 season. He was carted off with an air splint.Terry McLaurin injury and career statsAccording to Draft Sharks, Terry McLaurin suffered a non-contact left knee injury in the first quarter of Washington’s Week 6 game vs. San Francisco. He went down after running a route and grabbed at his knee. He was placed in an air cast and carted off the field.Just 17 days ago, the Ohio State alum suffered a grade 1 thigh/hamstring sprain/pull during practice. He had missed Week 4 vs. the Indianapolis Colts but was added in Week 5 vs. the New York Giants. In Week 6 vs. the San Francisco 49ers, he suffered a brutal knee injury that may end his season.As per Draft Sharks, McLaurin’s injury risk was low. He carried a 37% chance of injury in 2026, with a 2.7% chance of injury per game. He was projected to miss 2.1 games; he had already missed one in Week 4 and may now be out for the season. His durability was 5.00, with 5 being the highest possible.This season, the longtime Washington wide receiver recorded 15 receptions on 27 targets for 230 receiving yards and 1 touchdown in 5 games played. articles.title: Star Wars meets the NFL in Disney’s ambitious Super Bowl LXI plan, with live animation and iconic characters joining the game
articles.summary: Disney is giving Super Bowl LXI a twist that goes well beyond its usual halftime entertainment.
articles.body: Disney is giving Super Bowl LXI a twist that goes well beyond its usual halftime entertainment. ESPN, Lucasfilm, Disney and the NFL will present Star Wars Funday Football, an animated alternate broadcast that recreates every play of the February 14, 2027, championship game in real time. NFL players will appear as animated avatars inside the Star Wars universe, with familiar characters joining the action. The broadcast will stream on Disney+ and the ESPN App and air on Disney Channel and Disney XD. It will run alongside the traditional coverage from SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.Disney is bringing Star Wars characters into Super Bowl LXIThe project takes ESPN’s Funday Football concept to its biggest stage yet. Rather than simply adding Star Wars graphics to a regular broadcast, the production will recreate the game itself as an animated experience. Every play will be represented in real time, with players transformed into digital versions of themselves and franchise characters appearing at key moments.C-3PO and R2-D2 are already part of the promotional push. A teaser features the droids arriving on a desert planet, with Anthony Daniels returning to voice C-3PO, a role he has played since the original 1977 film.The technology behind the broadcast is central to the idea. Sony’s Beyond Sports will combine player-tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats with optical tracking from Sony’s Hawk-Eye Innovations to turn live action into animation. That means the presentation is designed to follow the actual game rather than show a pre-planned cartoon version of football.The final visual setting, additional characters and commentary details have yet to be announced. Those choices will help determine how closely the animated presentation follows the rhythm of the live contest.ESPN is expanding the crossover beyond the Super BowlDisney is not limiting the experiment to one Sunday. ESPN’s SC+ show on Disney+ will begin featuring Star Wars themed highlights from Monday Night Football on October 20, under the name “Hyperspace Highlights.”From October 26, the show will also feature an animated Darth Vader interviewing an NFL player taking part in that night’s Monday Night Football game. It gives ESPN another way to blend sports coverage with entertainment, using a recognisable character to draw viewers into weekly football discussions.The approach builds on earlier animated NFL presentations. ESPN, Disney and the league previously teamed up for Toy Story Funday Football in 2023, The Simpsons Funday Footballin 2024 and Monsters Funday Football in 2025. The *Toy Story* broadcast earned three Sports Emmy Awards.Super Bowl LXI marks a significant expansion because the format is moving from selected regular-season games to the NFL’s biggest annual event. The challenge is to make the animation appealing without losing the detail that serious fans expect from a live football broadcast.Fans will have several ways to watch the gameThe animated version will complement, not replace, the standard Super Bowl broadcast. ESPN and ABC will carry the main presentation, with Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge covering the game. Disney+ will stream the traditional broadcast for eligible US subscribers, while the animated version will have its own distribution across Disney+, the ESPN App, Disney Channel and Disney XD.The wider rollout also extends beyond the United States, with international availability planned across more than 155 markets through live broadcasts and on-demand access in selected regions. Additional viewing options will include the ManningCast with Peyton and Eli Manning, along with alternative coverage featuring Pat McAfee and Next Gen Stats.The timing also connects the project to Star Wars’ 50th anniversary. The original film is scheduled to return to theaters in a newly restored version on February 19, five days after the Super Bowl.For ESPN, the broadcast is a test of how far an alternate presentation can go without competing with the game itself. Football remains the main event. This time, though, viewers will be able to watch it unfold in a galaxy far, far away.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Dak Prescott, the Dallas Cowboys’ star quarterback, has recorded a pretty slow run on the field in the new season as the team has continued to struggle.
articles.body: Dak Prescott, the Dallas Cowboys’ star quarterback, has recorded a pretty slow run on the field in the new season as the team has continued to struggle. The Dallas Cowboys brutal loss against the Green Bay Packers marked their 4th loss in the new season as the team has managed to win just two games so far. The recent loss has sparked outrage among analysts even as Dak Pescott spoke about it.Dak Prescott addresses the Dallas Cowboys’ brutal performance on the field amid immense anger from analysts and fansA few hours ago, at a post game interview, Dak Prescott reflected on his performance as he said, “The defense, to me, played a good enough game for us to go out there and win this, and we just didn’t hold our own on offense, and that’s what ultimately sucks about it,” Prescott admitted postgame.The star quarterback added, “But that’s the NFL, and we’ve got to figure out a way to get better, and to get out of this rut, hole or whatever it is that we’ve been in these last two games.”But it seems it did not make the situation any better for the analysts,Jon Machota of The Athletic pointed to that disconnect, writing, “There’s too much talent on the Cowboys’ offense to look this bad. Everything is difficult for them tonight, just like last week against Tampa Bay. Makes no sense.”The Dallas Cowboys analyst RJ Ochoa wrote, “Obviously we are all mad, but I think it is telling that most (from what I see) Cowboys fans aren’t MAD the way you should be after a loss. Everyone is so down/out/embarrassed by this team. The last 3 seasons have been really hard/toxic/not fun. It takes a toll.”The Dallas Cowboys’ head coach Matt LaFleur reflected on it as he said, "At the end of the day, you just want it to be called both ways…If they're going to call it one way, it should be called for the other team as well. I feel like there have been a lot of times when Jordan's taken some hits that were close to drawing a penalty, but he's not getting the calls."In the ongoing 2026 NFL season, Dak Prescott has thrown for 1,639 passing yards, 10 touchdowns, and 5 interceptions with a 66.3% completion percentage across 6 games.This has marked a significant dip from Dak Prescott’s performance during the 2025 regular season, where he started all 17 games and accumulated 4,552 passing yards, 30 passing touchdowns, and 10 interceptions with a 67.3% completion rate and a 99.5 passer rating.For now, all eyes remain on the Week 7 clash.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Peyton Manning back in Indianapolis? Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s Colts could explore Hall of Famer for GM job to replace midseason fired general manager Chris Ballard
articles.summary: Now that’s a full circle.
articles.body: Now that’s a full circle. Peyton Manning began his NFL journey playing for the Indianapolis Colts, and now he could be back with the Colts - as their general manager in a front-office role.This move comes after the midseason dismissal of Chris Ballard, who had been with the Colts for nearly a decade since January 2017.Indianapolis owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, who has been busy taking notes on the sideline, could have made a shocking turn for the franchise - nobody saw it coming. Most fans are happy. Still, she’d be giving up on someone her late father, Jim Irsay, wholeheartedly believed in for years.Anyhow, the Peyton Manning rumors don’t just end at the front office doorstep. He could possibly acquire an ownership stake.Carlie Irsay-Gordon is hunting for a new GM; Manning fits the bill, but an ownership stake adds a completely different angle to it. That’s like asking a general manager to pour your heart and soul into the game because now you own it - not just owe it, but own-own it!Peyton Manning Colts GM rumorsAccording to The Dan Patrick Show, the Indianapolis Colts could contact Peyton Manning to discuss his keen interest in the franchise’s top executive position.He would be the very first person evaluated for the vacancy and considered for the general manager role. However, NBC Sports reported that the Colts had not yet contacted Manning at the time of publication.Manning, a Pro Football Hall of Famer, earned a Bachelor of Arts in speech communication from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.He spent his first 13 seasons with the Indianapolis Colts, leading the franchise to a victory in Super Bowl XLI and becoming one of the most influential players in its history. He finished his playing career with the Denver Broncos, retiring after winning Super Bowl 50, and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2021.Who did Peyton Manning play forPeyton Manning played college football for the Tennessee Volunteers at the University of Tennessee from 1994 to 1997.The legendary quarterback played in the NFL for the Indianapolis Colts from 1998 to 2010 and the Denver Broncos from 2012 to 2015. He won two Super Bowls - one for the Colts and one for the Broncos.The Colts drafted him in the 1998 NFL Draft as their first-round, first-overall pick. If he becomes the GM for the franchise, there would literally be no better candidate than someone who has represented/played for the franchise for years together.Chris Ballard fired after Indianapolis strugglesChris Ballard’s sudden midseason firing came following Indianapolis’ 26-20 loss to the winless Tennessee Titans. This could have left a sour taste in owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s mouth. So many teams defeated the Titans; why couldn’t the Colts?Anyhow, the shocking defeat left the Colts with a 2-4 season record. This thoroughly prompted owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon to make a leadership change.Usually, it’s the head coach, the offensive coordinator, or some players. But here, it’s a general manager - the highest of the highest authority. It makes one wonder - the head coach has been communicative with Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon on the gridiron, and the GM wasn’t?Anyhow, Ballard has served as the Colts’ general manager since 2017. He saw two playoff appearances happen but failed to achieve postseason success. The team missed the playoffs in all five seasons before his dismissal in October 2026.CBS Sports jotted down several reasons why Chris Ballard could have been fired. From failing to find a long-term solution at quarterback after Andrew Luck’s retirement to selecting Anthony Richardson.Also, trading two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner in November 2025.Indianapolis also committed $88 million to Daniel Jones in a two-year extension, thereby adding financial pressure on the front office to deliver results.Irsay-Gordon has regularly emphasized the urgency of returning Indianapolis to championship contention. Her first step toward that much-coveted change is firing Chris Ballard.Peyton Manning’s NFL return remains uncertainA lot of excitement surrounds a potential return of Peyton Manning to the NFL after his playing career.Since retiring, he has pursued successful media and business ventures, such as Omaha Productions and the ManningCast. If he takes on an NFL front-office role, he may have to give up on these media and business commitments.However, for the Indianapolis Colts, Manning could provide a major boost. articles.title: Veteran Free Agents Who Could Put Top NFL Contenders Over the Top After Week 6
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is coming up, but trades aren't the only option teams have to improve their rosters at this time.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is coming up, but trades aren't the only option teams have to improve their rosters at this time.

There is still a surprising amount of talent lingering in free agency deep into October, players who could make a real impact for contending franchises.

While these veterans may be coming off serious injuries or past their prime, they could still make meaningful contributions. They may also be relatively inexpensive to sign, as some players still seeking a team at this stage of the season could be willing to accept modest deals for a chance to chase a ring.

With that in mind, let's pair the top five Super Bowl contenders (based on the latest FanDuel Sportsbook odds) with a veteran free agent who could push them over the top.

Although they suffered a disheartening defeat against the Cleveland Browns this past weekend, the Baltimore Ravens remain a top Super Bowl contender.

With Lamar Jackson set to return soon from a brief injury-related absence, the team has some ground to make up in what has become a tight AFC North race.

One way to help the team avoid missing the playoffs for a second consecutive year is to improve the offense—specifically a passing attack that has become one-dimensional and overly reliant on star wideout Zay Flowers. Bringing in a reliable pass-catcher like Darius Slayton would bolster the receiving corps and give Jackson another option when the team needs a big play.

Despite missing one game and playing just 61 percent of Baltimore's offensive snaps in his five appearances because of a nagging hamstring injury, Flowers leads the team by a wide margin in receptions (32), targets (42) and receiving yards (471). He also leads the team with two receiving touchdowns.

Rashod Bateman, who has 16 catches for 233 yards and a touchdown on 22 targets, is the only other Ravens wide receiver with more than five catches, eight targets and 75 receiving yards this season. However, he exited Week 6 with a shoulder injury.

Rookie Ja'Kobi Lane had a promising training camp, but injuries have limited him to just two appearances so far. Fellow rookie Elijah Sarratt has been a healthy scratch most weeks, while Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are little more than depth options at this point.

Slayton can provide a wealth of experience stemming from his seven years with the New York Giants. He was steadily productive for much of that span, posting career totals of 4,435 receiving yards and 22 touchdowns on 296 receptions across 106 games.

While the Indianapolis Colts brought Slayton in to pad out their receiving depth last month, his brief tenure with the collapsing club ended with his release on October 16. The Ravens should capitalize on this surprise availability, adding a grizzled veteran who could play an immediate role for their short-handed offense.

The Buffalo Bills know they have a cornerback problem and are working to address it.

The team just signed Tre'Davious White to its practice squad, bringing him back for a third stint with the franchise since selecting him on Day 1 of the 2017 draft—but the Bills shouldn't be done making moves quite yet.

Bringing in Marshon Lattimore, another proven Pro Bowler with a wealth of experience, could be what this team needs to get back on track.

A massive overhaul in the secondary has become necessary after Buffalo got torched by several opposing passers to open the 2026 campaign. The defense ranks No. 31 in pass defense, allowing a concerning average of 285.8 yards per game through the air and recording just three interceptions over the first six weeks.

Buffalo's struggles have not come as a major surprise. The cornerback position looked thin on cutdown day, when the team elected to open the year with just three traditional outside corners on their final roster. One of them, 2025 first-rounder Maxwell Hairston, has been a disappointment and has seen a major reduction in playing time after making several mistakes over the first month of the campaign.

Lattimore could be a plug-and-play starter, as he was one of the league's top corners between 2017-2021—earning four Pro Bowl nods in that span. While injuries have limited his availability and effectiveness in recent years, it's been almost a year since he tore his ACL. If he's ready to contribute at a high level again, the Bills shouldn't hesitate to sign him.

Prior to his most recent knee injury, Lattimore had recorded 27 tackles, seven pass defenses and an interception in nine games for the Washington Commanders. Although his speed and athleticism have slipped, the 30-year-old still has the size and strength to work as a press corner in Buffalo's scheme.

The Kansas City Chiefs have reemerged as a Super Bowl contender after last year's disappointing season. They are the last remaining unbeaten team in the AFC and look like a lock to make the playoffs for the 10th time in 11 seasons, but there is still room for this perennial powerhouse to improve.

Adding experienced edge-rusher Haason Reddick to the mix could push the defense over the top.

One of the most glaring issues the Chiefs have been facing is a lack of pass-rushing power. They have recorded just eight sacks on the season, tied for the second-fewest in the league. Half of those came on Sunday, when they took advantage of a banged-up Los Angeles Chargers team that was starting four unproven rookies along the offensive line.

While it was promising to see Kansas City's edge-rushers finally clamp down on an opposing quarterback, the unit hasn't been getting home against better protection. Prior to Week 6, the Chiefs ranked a meager 27th in pass-rush win rate and broke through pass protection within 2.5 seconds at a 45 percent clip.

Reddick was one of the NFL's most productive pass-rushers between the 2020-2023 seasons, a four-season stretch in which he tallied a whopping 50.5 sacks despite suiting up for three different organizations. While his production dipped significantly over the last two years—he's recorded just 3.5 sacks since the start of the 2024 campaign—he could return to form in Kansas City.

The two-time Pro Bowler turned 32 last month, but he should still have some tread left on his tires. He could thrive as a part-time rotational piece in defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's system, helping the unit generate waves of pressure while its starters are getting a much-needed breather.

With an experienced, veteran-laden roster and an opportunity to compete for a Super Bowl, Kansas City could be a strong fit for Reddick.

The Los Angeles Rams remain a Super Bowl favorite despite a shocking stumble out of the gate in 2026. While the team still has the type of elite talent required to recover from an abysmal 2-4 start, the recent loss of Davante Adams was a major blow.

With Adams expected to miss six to 10 weeks while he recovers from a ruptured hamstring, the Rams need to offset the loss of their star wideout with a pickup on the open market. No free agent can move the needle more than Tyreek Hill.

Adams had been one of the bright spots for L.A. this season, recording 30 catches, 480 receiving yards and four touchdowns through six games—production that will be difficult for a midseason free-agent addition to replace.

Hill's résumé makes him an intriguing potential replacement, although his recovery and lengthy absence create uncertainty about how quickly he could contribute.

The eight-time Pro Bowler has been out of football since suffering a devastating knee injury early in the 2025 season, but agent Drew Rosenhaus revealed last week that his client is close to being able to return to action.

If healthy, his speed, route-running and elusiveness could help Los Angeles replace some of Adams' production.

After helping to establish the Kansas City Chiefs' dynasty early in his career, Hill took his game to another level following a trade to the Miami Dolphins in 2022.

The wideout posted back-to-back seasons with at least 1,700 yards, including making a legitimate run at Calvin Johnson's single-season yardage record during his 119-catch, 1,799-yard, 13-touchdown season in 2023.

While Hill declined in 2024—failing to reach the 1,000-yard receiving mark for the first time in any season he started at least 13 games in—and tore multiple knee ligaments the following year, his unique blend of speed, hands, route-running skills and elusiveness will greatly assist a championship hopeful.

The San Francisco 49ers are looking like the league's best team, remaining undefeated while becoming the first to reach six wins by toppling the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football.

The Niners are cruising towards the NFC West crown, but they can't rest on their laurels in what remains arguably the league's toughest division.

While San Francisco features a top-five defense, it hasn't generated pressure on a consistent basis. An extended absence from top edge-rusher Nick Bosa—who has been dealing with a calf injury since Week 2—has hindered the team's ability to get after opposing quarterbacks. San Francisco has tallied 15 sacks on the year, a league-average mark that needs improvement.

Considering how important pressure is in the modern NFL, especially against the elite passers teams inevitably come up against in the playoffs, the Niners would be wise to bolster their edge-rushing unit with one of the best available free agents: Joey Bosa.

While ESPN's Adam Schefter noted during the offseason that Bosa was " leaning towards retirement " rather than play an 11th NFL season in 2026, an opportunity to finish out his career with a Super Bowl ring earned alongside his younger brother might convince him to change those plans.

If San Francisco does bring in the older Bosa brother, it would mark the first time since a 2012 high school season that both Nick and Joey would play for the same team.

Even at the age of 31 with a history of injury, Joey Bosa can still be a force. He tallied five sacks, nine tackles for a loss, 16 quarterback hits and a league-leading five forced fumbles in 15 games with the Buffalo Bills last year and could be a key rotational piece for San Francisco in the back half of 2026.

articles.title: Titans release DT Jordan Elliott following undisclosed incident at team facility that occurred days before Week 6 win
articles.summary: The decision to part with Elliott was universally agreed upon, according to an ESPN report, which also noted the NFL is aware of the situation.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans revealed Tuesday they released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott in the wake of an undisclosed incident at the team facility.

The incident took place last Thursday, three days prior to the Titans notching their first win of the season, according to a statement from the organization.

"Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster," the statement read, via Titans team reporter Jim Wyatt.

"We will have no further comment on the matter."

Specifics of the incident have yet to be reported. But the decision to part with Elliott was universally agreed upon, according to an ESPN report , which also noted the NFL is aware of the situation.

Before practice this past Friday, Titans head coach Robert Saleh told reporters that Elliott wouldn't be available to participate that day because he was "dealing with personal stuff," per ESPN. He reportedly didn't travel with the team to Indianapolis on Saturday.

Elliott was among the inactive players the Titans announced ahead of their 26-20 triumph against the Colts.

Not only was the victory Tennessee's first of the 2026 campaign, but it was also the last straw for Colts ownership, which moved on from longtime general manager Chris Ballard in the fallout of that disheartening setback at home .

As for Elliott, the 28-year-old defensive lineman is in his seventh NFL season.

The Cleveland Browns selected him in the third round out of Missouri during the 2020 draft. He spent four seasons with the Browns, maxing out with 36 total tackles — including five for loss — in 2022. Then he went to San Francisco, where he was a consistent starter for the 49ers. In his two seasons with the Niners, Elliott started 29 of the 31 games he played.

This past offseason, the Titans signed Elliott to a two-year deal reportedly worth up to $8.5 million. He made five appearances with Tennessee, including one start.

Along the way, he recorded 11 total tackles and, per Pro Football Focus, 114 defensive snaps. In his absence over the weekend, Timmy Horne was elevated from the practice squad and played 25 defensive snaps, according to PFF.

articles.title: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson’s love story: How a chance meeting turned into a romance that captivated the sports world
articles.summary: Bill Belichick has spent decades making history in the NFL, winning six Super Bowls as head coach of the New England Patriots.
articles.body: Bill Belichick has spent decades making history in the NFL, winning six Super Bowls as head coach of the New England Patriots. But one unexpected meeting outside the football world brought a new chapter into his personal life. His relationship with Jordon Hudson began with a conversation on a flight in 2021 and later grew into a romance that attracted attention across the sports world. With a 48-year age difference, their relationship has faced plenty of questions, headlines, and public scrutiny. Yet, from their early connection to public appearances and the support Hudson has shown Belichick during his move to college football, their story has continued to unfold in the public eye. As of October 2026, they have known each other for about five years, although reports place the beginning of their romantic relationship around 2023.How did Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson first meet in 2021?Their story began in February 2021, when Belichick and Hudson reportedly met on a flight from Massachusetts to Florida. At the time, Belichick was already one of football’s most successful coaches, while Hudson was a college student and competitive cheerleader at Bridgewater State University.According to accounts they later shared, the two began talking after Belichick noticed the philosophy textbook Hudson was reading. The book was Deductive Logic, and their conversation about it gave them an unusual starting point.Belichick signed her textbook with a message that read, “Thanks for giving me a course in logic! Safe travels!” He also included his signature and references to the years the Patriots had won the Super Bowl. Hudson later shared a picture of the inscription on social media, offering a glimpse of their first meeting.It was a simple exchange, and there was no public confirmation at the time that it would lead to a romantic relationship. Their meeting happened years before the public became interested in their personal lives, making that signed textbook a small but memorable part of their story.When did their friendship turn into a romantic relationship?Although Belichick and Hudson met in 2021, their romantic relationship reportedly began in early 2023. The pair were spotted together on several occasions that year, including outings in New Orleans, which led to growing speculation about their connection. However, neither publicly shared a detailed account of when their relationship changed from their initial meeting into romance.Their relationship became public knowledge in June 2024, when reports confirmed they were dating. Hudson also began responding to comments about their age difference, showing that she was aware of the attention their relationship was attracting.For Belichick, who had spent much of his career keeping his private life away from the spotlight, the attention was a major change. His previous long-term relationship with Linda Holliday ended in 2023 after more than a decade together. His relationship with Hudson soon became a regular subject of sports and entertainment coverage.In October 2024, Hudson made their relationship Instagram official by sharing photographs of the couple. It was a clear public step for a pair who had largely kept their connection out of view during its early years.How did Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson make their relationship public?By late 2024, the couple were appearing together at major events. One of their most notable appearances came in December, when they attended the Museum Gala at the American Museum of Natural History in New York. Their red-carpet appearance gave the public another look at a relationship that had become increasingly difficult to keep private.Their age difference became a frequent topic of conversation, with Belichick nearly 49 years older than Hudson. Some of the attention was lighthearted, while other reactions were more critical. Their relationship was even joked about during the 2024 Netflix special The Roast of Tom Brady, where the difference in their ages became part of the comedy.But public interest was not limited to their romance. Hudson also became involved in some of Belichick’s business matters outside football. In his 2025 memoir, The Art of Winning: Lessons from My Life in Football, Belichick described her as his “idea mill and creative muse.” He later explained that she had helped with the business side of the book and offered a fresh perspective when his writing became too technical.Their relationship attracted further attention in April 2025, when Hudson interrupted a CBS interview as Belichick was asked how they had met. Belichick later defended her, explaining that she had been trying to keep the discussion focused on his book. CBS, however, said the interview had been agreed upon as a wide-ranging conversation without restrictions on the topics. The incident became one of the most talked-about moments in their public relationship.What does their relationship look like in october 2026?By October 2026, Belichick and Hudson had known each other for around five years, while their reported romantic relationship had lasted approximately three years. Their story had moved well beyond the chance meeting on a flight, with Hudson continuing to appear alongside Belichick during his new chapter as head coach of the University of North Carolina.Their relationship has also faced questions about Hudson’s involvement in football matters. In September 2026, Belichick pushed back against suggestions that she had a role in UNC’s football operations, making a distinction between their personal relationship, her help with outside business matters, and the running of his team.Most recently, Hudson was seen supporting Belichick as North Carolina defeated Duke 24-20 on October 17, 2026. The victory was a notable moment for Belichick and his team, and Hudson was present as he celebrated the result.Their relationship has never been free from public discussion, and much of their private life remains just that, private. They have not shared every detail of their journey, so it would be unfair to assume what their connection means to them beyond what they have said and shown publicly.Still, their story has come a long way from a conversation about a philosophy textbook on a flight. From their reported romance in 2023 to making their relationship public in 2024 and facing intense scrutiny in the years that followed, Belichick and Hudson have continued to build a life together under the spotlight. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s pain tolerance becomes the talking point as ex-Chiefs WR delivers a blunt assessment
articles.summary: Travis Kelce hurt his right ankle on Kansas City's opening drive against the Chargers and still finished the game with 53 receiving yards.
articles.body: Travis Kelce hurt his right ankle on Kansas City's opening drive against the Chargers and still finished the game with 53 receiving yards. The Chiefs tight end twisted the ankle on a screen pass, got it taped on the sideline, and came back. Kansas City beat winless Los Angeles, which dropped to 0-6. The Chiefs won on the ground and on defense, yet the ankle drew most of the attention. Ex-Chiefs receiver Dieter praised the effort on X, and Andy Reid backed it up after the game. Whether Kelce is healthy for Seattle is the next question.Travis Kelce's pain tolerance draws praise from an ex-Chiefs receiverThe injury came early. Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley tackled Kelce after a screen pass, and his right ankle appeared to twist as he went down. He limped to the sideline, had it checked and taped, and went back in. Dieter, a former Chiefs wide receiver, summed it up on X."Kelce is a dawg! They don't make em like him anymore. Anyone else would be milking that ankle injury."He has a point. Kelce is 37 and presumably in his final season, yet he is still producing. That is not a small thing at his age. He has already moved past Jason Witten for second place on the NFL's all-time receiving yards list for tight ends, and he caught nine passes for 101 yards against the Colts. Reid even said this offseason that he had to "yank" Kelce out of practice because he works that hard.Reid kept his own review short after the game. "Kelce tweaked his ankle there but continued to play. It might be a little sore tomorrow, but he did a nice job tonight."Kansas City's win came from the ground and the defenseKansas City could not afford to lose another pass catcher. Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton were already unavailable, which made Kelce's return more than a show of grit. After he came back, he added a 24-yard gain on a pass from Patrick Mahomes.Still, Mahomes leaned on Xavier Worthy. Worthy caught all seven targets for 73 yards, the best total among Chiefs receivers. Seven for seven is rare.The run game led the way. Kenneth Walker III carried 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns, including a 33-yard score on the second drive. It was his fourth 100-yard game in five outings since he signed with Kansas City. Mahomes finished 23 of 30 for 272 yards, so the passing game was fine too.The defense was just as steady. Kansas City sacked Justin Herbert four times, with Ashton Gillotte, George Karlaftis and Chamarri Conner among those who got to him. The Chiefs outgained the Chargers 422 yards to 259, and Los Angeles had to settle for two field goals without a touchdown.Seattle is next, and the Chiefs will face the defending Super Bowl champions there. No diagnosis or timetable for Kelce had been announced as of late Sunday. The Republican governor, wearing a hoodie with the Saints' trademark fleur-de-lis symbol across his chest, left Louis Armstrong Airport on Monday evening. He spoke with reporters before boarding his flight "with a bunch of folks" who would spend the week in France before Sunday's NFL game between the Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers at Stade de France in Saint-Denis. articles.title: 49ers sputter in second half after Mike Evans' injury but hold on to beat Commanders to improve to 6-0
articles.summary: The 49ers had a big lead, but the Commanders got back in the game.
articles.body: At some point, the San Francisco 49ers' injuries might bring them down. It almost happened in the second half on Monday night. For now, San Francisco's perfect season rolls on. The 49ers raced out to a 20-point lead and it looked like they would cruise to an easy win over the Washington Commanders. But San Francisco's offense stalled with No. 1 receiver Mike Evans sidelined with an Achilles injury he suffered late in the first half, allowing the Commanders to get back in the game. The Niners' defense, which has been a big surprise all season, came up with two big stops in the final two minutes to seal the 23-17 win. The 49ers improved to 6-0 to start the season. Treylon Burks couldn't haul in a fourth-down pass at the goal line as safety Malik Mustapha, who made a huge hit on a run the previous play, slammed him to the ground. FANTASTIC PBU TO PREVENT THE TD ‼️WASvsSF on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hMlXf1fdwc— NFL (@NFL) October 20, 2026 Washington got one more shot after forcing a punt, but an intentional grounding penalty set the Commanders back and then the 49ers ended the game on a sack. Brock Purdy played well in the first half, as he has all season, but he needs some help. The 49ers are depleted at receiver and it showed in the second half. That allowed the Commanders to get back in it. Washington hurt themselves, particularly with a facemask penalty that negated a touchdown with a little more than four minutes remaining. Jeremy McNichols had a TD here that was wiped away from Chris Paul’s facemask penalty Heartbreaking pic.twitter.com/bvk5eSwiYt— brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 20, 2026 The 49ers look like the best team in football about one-third through the season. It has been a great start, but the injuries are becoming a real concern. The Niners have been the unluckiest team when it comes to injuries for a few seasons, and the bad fortune hasn't stopped. Mike Evans injured in first halfIt wouldn't be a 49ers game without a key injury. Evans, who came into the game with injuries to his ribs and Achilles tendon, left Monday night's game due to the Achilles. He stayed down after a catch late in the second quarter and went straight to the locker room with athletic trainers. He was ruled out of the game by the team.The 49ers are getting desperately thin at receiver and the injury to Evans, who has made an immediate impact on San Francisco's offense, would be a big blow if he has to miss time. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that he didn't expect the injury to be long-term.Still, it's still a lingering issue for a 33-year-old receiver. And a glimpse at the 49ers' offense without Evans wasn't pretty.The 49ers slowed down on offense in the second half without Evans and the Commanders got back in the game. Jayden Daniels hit Rachaad White on a touchdown pass with 9:22 left and suddenly Washington had cut San Francisco's lead to 23-17. San Francisco had led 23-3 late in the third quarter. The Commanders forced a quick punt after that and had the ball with a chance to take the lead with 7:46 to go. It looked like an easy night for the 49ers, but Washington was putting San Francisco's perfect record in jeopardy. Second half tightens upOnce Washington started getting momentum, the Commanders were hard to stop. Daniels hadn't had a great night, including strangely throwing the ball away on a fourth down in the first half, but he helped get his team back in the game. He did so without top receiver Terry McLaurin, who was lost in the first half when he was carted off due to a knee injury. The Commanders seemingly took the lead with a little more than four minutes left on a Jeremy McNichols touchdown run, but there was a facemask penalty on Washington guard Chris Paul that negated the score. The 49ers had a big penalty of their own later, when a fourth-down sack was wiped off the board due to an illegal contact penalty that gave Washington a first down. San Francisco came up with the plays it needed, with Mustapha having two big hits on third and fourth down. Washington wasn't finished. It forced a three-and-out and got the ball back with less than a minute to go, but no timeouts. A fair catch interference call helped with field position. The Commanders were running out of time but a 17-yard catch by rookie receiver Antonio Williams got the ball to San Francisco's 28-yard line. But an intentional grounding penalty on Daniels was a crushing blow, especially since there was a 10-second runoff, leaving only six seconds on the clock. A sack on the final play sealed the win.The 49ers survived a scare. Even a great season isn't always going to pretty. And it looks like it could be a memorable year for the 49ers. The injury issues might be the biggest threat to stopping them.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , former Alabama Crimson Tide running back Najee Harris has reportedly been released by the New York Giants.

Following the reported release, Harris will now be looking for his third NFL team in the last two seasons. Harris saw action in three games a year ago with the Los Angeles Chargers prior to suffering a season-ending injury.

articles.title: Report: Umpire Larry Smith out for season after slipping on Wembley Stadium grass
articles.summary: NFL official Larry Smith suffered a season-ending injury on Sunday in London.
articles.body:
NFL official Larry Smith suffered a season-ending injury on Sunday in London.

Smith, who serves as the umpire on referee Shawn Hochuli's crew, suffered a torn quadricep and is out for the season , according to FootballZebras.com.

Smith slipped on the wet grass at Wembley Stadium and fell on his back, tried to get up and fell again between plays. Trainers from both teams attended to him and he was eventually taken off the field on a cart. The officiating crew was down to six for the rest of the game, with other officials splitting the umpire's responsibilities.

This is Smith's first season officiating in the NFL after several seasons working in college football and spring leagues. Now he'll sit out and won't work another game until 2027.

The NFL will have to find a replacement umpire for Hochuli's crew for the rest of the season. The league always has some officials lined up who can join a crew during the season when needed.

articles.title: Giants could take advantage if Indianapolis Colts go into fire sale mode
articles.summary: Is Jonathan Taylor the Giants’ answer at running back?
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are 2-4 and fired general manager Chris Ballard this week. There is obvious speculation that the Colts could be in a break-it-down-and-start-over fire sale. The New York Giants could be a team to watch if the Colts go in that direction.

Below are my top three targets for the Giants if the Colts decide to be aggressive sellers—and the NFC East-leading Giants aggressive buyers—before the Nov. 10 NFL Trade Deadline.

This is the most obvious possibility. Giants head coach John Harbaugh is pining for " a Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance" at running back.

The Giants ended their four-way timeshare at running back on Tuesday by releasing Najee Harris . That doesn't mean that they have solved their running back issues. They don't have a 20-yard run from a running back yet this season. Cam Skattebo has averaged 3.6 yards per carry with four fumbles, Tyrone Tracy 3.1, and Devin Singletary 3.0. Blocking has been part of the issue , but none of the backs have distinguished themselves.

The 27-year-old is one of the game's elite backs and would immediately give Harbaugh and the Giants the Henry/Barkley circumstance Harbaugh spoke about.

Taylor has four 1,000-yard seasons over his first six NFL seasons, three Pro Bowl appearances, and a first-team All-Pro honor in 2021. Injuries limited him in 2022 and 2023, the only seasons he did not reach 1,000 yards.

Taylor had 1,585 yards rushing and a league-best 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025.

Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension with the Colts that runs through the 2028 season. He would cost an acquiring team the prorated portion of his 2026 salary, and roughly $34 million over the 2027 and 2028 seasons. His contract includes a 2028 out, with a $7.5 million roster bonus due on the fifth day of the 2028 league year.

What would it take to acquire Taylor? SB Nation's Stampede Blue believes a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 third-round pick would be an appropriate price tag.

Maybe that is an appropriate price tag. The Pro Football and Sports Network trade machine, though, thinks a fair price would involve the Giants surrendering a first-round pick in either 2027 or 2028 to go along with a Day 2 asset.

The 32-year-old is a free agent-to-be who has been one of the better defensive linemen in the NFL ever since the San Francisco 49ers made him a first-round pick in the 2016 NFL Draft. It wouldn't make any sense for the Colts not to make him available at the trade deadline.

The Giants are having success with long-in-the-tooth defensive linemen D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris, but haven't had much luck finding depth behind them. Buckner would take care of that issue. For now.

There are two problems. If Buckner is available, there figure to be several suitors. The other is cost.

A team acquiring Buckner would have to figure out how to fit $23 million of the $26 million he is earning this season under their cap.

I ran this through the PFSN trade simulator, and it told me that third-round picks in 2027 and 2028 AND Kayvon Thibodeaux might not be enough to get a deal done, and wouldn't quite get the Giants, with just over $8 million in cap space, under the cap.

This one is probably pie-in-the-sky. But, hey, we can talk about it.

The 30-year-old eight-time Pro Bowler (every year of his career) and three-time All-Pro is perhaps the best guard in the game. He is going to be in the Pro Football Hall of Fame one day. He remains an elite run blocker and very good pass blocker.

He is also in the final year of his contract.

Nelson would provide a massive upgrade to a Giants offensive line that has been struggling to run block.

Again, though, there are myriad problems in trying to trade for Nelson.

Giants left guard Jon Runyan Jr. is a good pass blocker, but a poor run blocker. The Giants, though, gave him a two-year, $22 million extension through 2028 that guarantees him $19.5 million. That's a lot of money to sit on the bench.

The PFSN trade simulator says it would take a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 first-rounder to get Nelson. It would also put them roughly $10 million over the salary cap, so they would have to figure that out.

That is not a trade you can make without getting Nelson to sign a long-term deal, and perhaps considering the idea of transitioning Runyan to center.

Are any of these trade possibilities appealing to you, Giants fans?

articles.title: Beyond charity, Russell Wilson and Ciara are building a brighter future for children with 3 youth centers and $5.5 million in gifts
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and Ciara have built successful careers in football and music, but their work away from the spotlight has also become an important part of
articles.body: Russell Wilson and Ciara have built successful careers in football and music, but their work away from the spotlight has also become an important part of their public lives. Through the Why Not You Foundation, which they founded in 2014, the couple supports children’s education, health care and efforts to fight poverty. Their recent work includes a $3 million gift to Mount Sinai Kravis Children’s Hospital in New York, a $500,000 contribution toward food assistance in Atlanta and a $2 million donation to the Los Cabos Children’s Foundation in Mexico. They have also supported youth centers and educational programs, although the closure of a school connected to their mission shows that creating lasting change can be difficult. These projects offer a closer look at how the NFL quarterback and singer are using their resources to support children and families.What is the Why Not You Foundation trying to achieve?Russell Wilson and Ciara established the Why Not You Foundation in 2014. The nonprofit focuses on education, children’s health, and fighting poverty. Its work also includes food security and programs designed to help girls and young women develop leadership skills.The foundation’s name comes from a question Wilson’s father used to ask him: “Why not you?” The message encouraged Wilson to believe in his abilities and consider what he could achieve. Today, the foundation uses the same idea to encourage young people to pursue opportunities and build confidence in their future.Its work covers several areas rather than focusing on a single cause. The foundation supports organizations and programs working with children, including Boys & Girls Clubs, Friends of the Children and the V Foundation for Cancer Research.This approach allows the foundation to support different needs, from education and mentorship to health care and food assistance. However, its overall impact cannot be measured by the number of causes it supports alone. Published figures on program participation, outcomes and long-term progress are also important when assessing how much difference these projects make.How are their donations supporting children’s health and families?One of the foundation’s major recent contributions came in November 2025, when Wilson and Ciara announced a $3 million gift to Mount Sinai Kravis Children’s Hospital in New York City. The donation supports patient and family programs, including therapeutic spaces for children receiving medical treatment.The gift includes support for the Child Life Zone Theater and Play Space in the Jack Martin Fund Inpatient Unit for Children’s Cancer and Blood Disease. These spaces are designed to give young patients opportunities to play and take part in activities during their hospital stays.The couple also directed funding toward children’s health services in Mexico. In February 2026, the foundation pledged $2 million to the Los Cabos Children’s Foundation in Baja California Sur. The donation is intended to expand health care, nutrition, preventive care and rehabilitation services for children and families.Food assistance is another part of the foundation’s work. In December 2025, it announced a $500,000 donation to the Atlanta Community Food Bank and ATL Cares to help families facing food insecurity. Reports at the time said the contribution was expected to provide more than one million additional meals during the holiday season.Together, these three announced gifts total $5.5 million. The amount covers the specific contributions announced for Mount Sinai, Atlanta food assistance and the Los Cabos Children’s Foundation. It does not represent the foundation’s total charitable spending.The donations also address different needs. The hospital gift supports children receiving treatment, the Mexico contribution focuses on health and rehabilitation services, and the Atlanta donation aims to help families access food.How are their youth centers creating opportunities for children?The Why Not You Foundation has also invested in community spaces where young people can access educational and recreational activities. Its published impact information lists three Why Not You Centers opened by 2025.The first center opened in Pittsburgh in 2024, followed by locations in Atlanta and Pasadena in 2025. The centers operate through partnerships with local Boys & Girls Clubs.Their programs include academic support, sports, creative activities and opportunities for personal development. The aim is to provide young people with access to resources and activities within their communities.Working with existing organizations also gives the foundation a way to support programs that already have local connections. Rather than creating an entirely separate network, the centers operate alongside community groups that provide services to children and young people.However, the number of centers does not tell the full story. Figures showing how many children attend, how often they participate and what results they achieve would help readers understand their direct impact. Those details are important when measuring whether the centers are meeting their goals.The foundation’s education work also includes Why Not You Academy, a tuition-free charter public high school in Des Moines, Washington. In 2020, Wilson and Ciara contributed approximately $1.75 million through their foundation to support the school’s launch and rebranding.The academy was designed to serve students facing barriers to educational opportunities and offered learning programs for grades nine through 12. At one point, enrollment reached nearly 200 students. However, the school later faced falling enrollment and financial and academic challenges.What does the closure of Why Not You Academy tell us?Why Not You Academy’s closure is an important part of the foundation’s educational record. Reports in 2025 showed that enrollment had fallen to 65 students. The school also faced concerns about attendance, graduation rates and its financial position.According to local reporting, the academy recorded a four-year graduation rate of 62%, while only 12% of students attended at least 90% of school days during the last reported academic year. These figures formed part of the wider concerns about the school’s performance.The school board voted to close the academy in November 2025, citing declining enrollment and concerns about its financial and operational position. The school subsequently closed at the end of the 2025–26 school year.The closure does not mean that all the foundation’s educational efforts have failed. Its youth centers and other partnerships continue to form part of its broader mission. However, the academy’s experience shows why donations alone cannot guarantee the long-term success of an educational project.Schools need stable enrollment, strong management, financial planning and consistent academic support. They also need to track attendance, graduation rates and student progress to understand whether their programs are working.For Wilson and Ciara, the foundation remains a way to direct resources toward children and families through education, health care and community programs. Its $5.5 million in recently announced gifts and three youth centers opened by 2025 provide measurable examples of that work.The next important measure will be the results these projects achieve over time. Information about the number of children served, improvements in access to care and education, and the long-term performance of community programs will help show how effectively the foundation is meeting its goals. articles.title: Caitlin Clark joins Taylor Swift at Chiefs game
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark is making the most of her basketball offseason by returning to Arrowhead Stadium and cheering for her longtime favorite NFL team. The Indiana F...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark traded the basketball court for an NFL Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium, joining Taylor Swift in a suite as the Kansas City Chiefs faced the Los Angeles Chargers. The Indiana Fever star had plenty to celebrate by the final whistle.

Kansas City defeated Los Angeles 22-6, improving to 5-0 and continuing its unbeaten start. Clark was spotted enjoying the action alongside Swift and sisters Este and Alana Haim as the Chiefs controlled another home game.

For Clark, the appearance came shortly after the Fever's WNBA season ended in the playoffs. With basketball responsibilities temporarily behind her, the 24-year-old returned to a familiar role away from the court: cheering for the Chiefs.

Clark joins Swift for Chiefs-Chargers matchup

Clark watched the Oct. 18 matchup from a suite at Arrowhead Stadium, where Swift was supporting Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce. Este and Alana Haim were also seen with the group during the game.

The appearance brought together 2 stars whose connections to Kansas City football have been well documented. Swift has regularly attended Chiefs games, while Clark has spoken publicly about following the team long before becoming one of basketball's biggest names.

Clark appeared relaxed as she followed the game from the suite. After months built around practices, travel and high-pressure WNBA games, the NFL outing gave her an opportunity to enjoy sports without being the athlete responsible for the result.

Kansas City gives Clark plenty to celebrate

The Chiefs handled the Chargers 22-6 at Arrowhead, moving to 5-0. Kansas City entered its bye undefeated and returned without losing momentum, holding Los Angeles to 6 points in a convincing divisional victory.

Kansas City's defense kept the Chargers from reaching the end zone. The result followed victories over Denver, Indianapolis, Miami and Las Vegas, leaving the Chiefs perfect through their opening 5 games of the regular season.

Clark has experienced plenty of high-pressure environments herself, but this time she could simply react as a fan. The Chiefs' strong start has provided supporters with an encouraging opening stretch as the NFL schedule moves deeper into the fall.

Clark has a long connection to the Chiefs

Clark's appearance was hardly a case of a celebrity choosing a successful NFL team for a weekend outing. She grew up in West Des Moines, Iowa, and has repeatedly identified herself as a longtime Chiefs supporter.

Her connection with the franchise became especially visible in January 2025, when she attended Kansas City's divisional-round playoff victory over the Houston Texans. Clark watched that game from a suite with Swift as the Chiefs advanced.

That history makes her latest Arrowhead visit a continuation rather than a surprise. Clark may spend her professional basketball season representing Indianapolis, but Kansas City remains the NFL team she has followed through different stages of her life and career.

The outing follows another big season for Clark

Clark entered her NFL break after producing her strongest WNBA season yet. She averaged 22.3 points, 8.3 assists and 4.0 rebounds across 40 regular-season appearances for Indiana while shooting 44.5% from the field.

Her playmaking remained one of her defining strengths. Clark finished second in the league with 8.3 assists per game while ranking third in scoring, combining her passing range with increased efficiency as a scorer during her third professional season.

Clark also averaged 2.9 made 3-pointers per game and shot 36.1% from beyond the arc. Her combination of scoring and passing helped Indiana produce a league-record 96.0 points per game during the regular season.

Indiana's playoff run extended Clark's year

Clark's basketball schedule stretched into the fall because Indiana reached the WNBA playoffs. The Fever eventually saw their season end against the Las Vegas Aces after competing in a postseason series that required Clark and her teammates to navigate elimination pressure.

One of Clark's biggest playoff performances came when Indiana needed it most. Facing elimination at home, she opened Game 2 against Las Vegas with a deep 3-pointer and helped the Fever force another game in the series.

The playoff exit created an immediate change of pace. Instead of preparing for another basketball opponent, Clark could turn her attention toward rest and recovery, making an NFL weekend at Arrowhead a natural offseason activity for a longtime Chiefs supporter.

Clark and Swift share another Arrowhead moment

Clark and Swift watched the Chiefs together on Oct. 12, 2025, when Kansas City faced the Detroit Lions at Arrowhead Stadium. Television cameras showed the two chatting and smiling in a suite during the game.

Their latest appearance arrived under different circumstances. Clark is now deeper into her WNBA career, while Swift continued her regular presence at Chiefs home games in support of Kelce during Kansas City's unbeaten start to the season.

The suite naturally attracted attention because of the recognizable names inside it, but Clark's presence fit her established football fandom. She has never needed a basketball connection to Kansas City to explain why she keeps returning to Arrowhead.

Clark's competitive calendar has remained demanding since entering the WNBA. Regular-season games, postseason basketball, practices, travel and the attention surrounding her performances leave relatively limited stretches in which basketball is not the immediate priority.

The offseason provides a valuable change of rhythm. Clark can step away from nightly WNBA competition before preparations begin for another season with Indiana, where expectations will remain high following her continued individual development and the Fever's recent playoff experience.

Watching the Chiefs offers a different kind of sporting experience. Clark can follow the action as a supporter rather than controlling possessions herself, and Kansas City's 5-0 opening has given her plenty to enjoy during the early portion of her basketball offseason.

Clark's Chiefs fandom keeps producing memorable moments

Clark's latest trip to Arrowhead adds another chapter to a connection that predates her professional career. Her profile has changed dramatically, but her willingness to publicly support Kansas City has remained consistent as her own sports career has grown.

Her support for the Chiefs also highlights how sports connect athletes beyond their own leagues. While Clark spends her season competing in the WNBA, following Kansas City gives her another way to enjoy elite competition and share memorable sporting moments with fellow fans.

There will be plenty of basketball waiting when Clark turns her full attention toward another Fever season. For now, she can enjoy being part of the crowd, following an undefeated Chiefs team and experiencing football from the other side of the spotlight.

Fun fact: Caitlin Clark's family had a Kansas City Chiefs-themed vending machine in their basement when she was growing up. She also wore toy Chiefs helmets while playing with her brothers, showing that her team loyalty began long before her WNBA fame.
