articles.title: Former NFL Punter Kasey Redfern Dies at 35 After Being Diagnosed with Rare Form of Cancer
articles.summary: Former NFL punter Kasey Redfern died last week at the age of 35 after being diagnosed with a rare form of cancer in 2023.
articles.body:
Former NFL punter Kasey Redfern died last week at the age of 35 after being diagnosed with a rare form of cancer in 2023.

According to Redfern's obituary , he died in Spartanburg, South Carolina, on Oct. 13 as a result of central nervous system lymphoma.

After playing collegiately at Wofford College, Redfern bounced around between multiple NFL teams from 2014 to 2019.

He appeared in a total of four NFL regular-season games, punting in one contest for the Detroit Lions in 2017, and three games for the Atlanta Falcons in 2019.

On 10 career punts, Redfern averaged 42.1 yards per attempt with three punts downed inside the 20. He also had nine touchbacks on 16 kickoffs.

In addition to his stints in Detroit and Atlanta, Redfern spent time with the Jacksonville Jaguars, San Diego Chargers, Carolina Panthers, Cleveland Browns and Dallas Cowboys as part of their preseason rosters or practice squads.

Before a football coach discovered him in high school, Redfern played soccer as a goalkeeper and was part of the U17-U18 U.S. Soccer Development Academy, per his obituary.

Redfern is survived by his wife and two sons, as well as his parents and two brothers.

articles.title: Eagles Won't Be Disciplined for Handling of Jalen Hurts' Blood Clot, NFLPA Calls for Investigation
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles will not face any discipline from the NFL over their handling of Jalen Hurts' injury reporting and the medical process regarding his blood clot diagnosis.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will not face any discipline from the NFL over their handling of Jalen Hurts' injury reporting and the medical process regarding his blood clot diagnosis.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the NFL has concluded its investigation into the situation and won't issue any discipline to the Eagles.

The NFLPA responded with its own statement calling for a "full investigation."

Hurts was added to Philadelphia's Week 5 injury report on Friday with what was labeled a calf injury, but he was a full participant in practice that day and played the entire game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

The club announced on Oct. 15 that Hurts injured his calf when he took a cleat to the area during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The day before the Jaguars game after their flight to London and a walkthrough, he had an ultrasound that revealed a superficial blood clot in his calf.

According to Jones, "Allen Sills, the NFL's chief medical doctor, arranged with Mark Gillett, the chief medical officer of the Premier League, to have Hurts seen at the Cleveland Clinic in London on Saturday night following a team walkthrough. That is where the superficial blood clot in Hurts' calf was first discovered, and the source says that the team, staff, doctors and Hurts made the determination that he could play the following day against the Jaguars."

A follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday showed the blood clot in Hurts' calf had moved.

As a result, Hurts was held out of Philadelphia's game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. A joint statement from the Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released on Monday announced Hurts would likely miss the remainder of the season after additional testing showed he had blood clots in his lungs.

The statement adds Hurts is expected to make a full recovery and he will be able to resume his NFL career when he comes off blood thinners.

This season will mark the first time since entering the NFL that Hurts will miss more than two games. He appeared in 15 games as a rookie in 2020 and started at least 15 games from 2021 to '25.

Tanner McKee, who got the starting nod against the Panthers, will remain the No. 1 quarterback on Sunday when the Eagles host the Dallas Cowboys.

articles.title: At Least $963K in Trading Cards Were Stolen from a FedEx Truck in California
articles.summary: SANTA ANA, Calif. (AP) — Police in California are investigating the theft of trading cards worth at least $963,000 that were taken from a FedEx truck parked outside of a company that verifies memorabilia.
articles.body:
SANTA ANA, Calif. (AP) — Police in California are investigating the theft of trading cards worth at least $963,000 that were taken from a FedEx truck parked outside of a company that verifies memorabilia.

The truck was broken into on Oct. 13 near Professional Sports Authenticator, also known as PSA, which authenticates trading cards, autographs, comic books, and other memorabilia and grades their condition, Santa Ana Police Department spokesperson Natalie Garcia said in a news release. Pokémon and sports cards were among the items that were stolen, the release said.

The driver had left the truck unattended, Garcia said in a follow-up email Tuesday. How long the driver was gone is part of the investigation, she said.

The truck's lock was gone and two pallets were taken, she said. A third pallet was disturbed.

"The estimated value of the stolen cards at the time of the incident was $963,000. However, the exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined," Garcia said in the news release.

Nick Andrews, a card collector near Boston, told The Associated Press the value of what was taken could be much higher.

PSA's parent company, Collectors, said it has "deactivated the certificates for the stolen cards and notified marketplace partners so they can be on the lookout for rare and serialized items."

The company also said it contacted affected customers directly and arranged for compensation based on fair market value.

Both FedEx and Collectors said they are working with law enforcement.

"The security of our customers' shipments is a top priority," FedEx spokesperson David Westrick said in a statement.

FedEx referred additional questions to police.

Some people who identified themselves as customers posted online that they got an email from PSA explaining what happened to their cards. They were worried they would never see them again or receive proper compensation.

Andrews, who collects vintage sports and Pokémon cards, told the AP in a phone interview that he was not affected by the theft but has heard from at least two dozen people who were.

"Thousands of cards, most likely, and millions of dollars, most likely," he said of the losses collectors suffered.

He said one person who submitted cards for grading on behalf of several people told him that they lost half a million dollars in declared value.

PSA's parent company did not get into specifics on losses in its statement.

"We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset," the statement from Collectors said. "Our team is focused on supporting them. We take this incident seriously, and we will continue working with law enforcement to hold those responsible accountable."

articles.title: Terry McLaurin Injured, Latest Updates After Commanders WR Was Carted Off vs. 49ers
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders will be without wide receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders will be without wide receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season.

Head coach Dan Quinn told reporters on Tuesday that McLaurin tore his patellar tendon Monday night and will undergo season-ending surgery.

McLaurin suffered the injury when he got tangled up with cornerback Deommodore Lenoir and grabbed at his knee as he was falling to the ground. McLaurin was carted off the field with an air cast on his leg.

He was officially ruled out with a knee injury shortly after coming out of the game.

The two-time Pro Bowler is one of Washington's veteran leaders and will be nearly impossible to replace.

McLaurin surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in five straight seasons from 2020 through 2024 before injuries limited him to just 10 games in 2025. He also missed the Commanders' Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts because of a hamstring injury.

However, he returned for the next contest against the New York Giants and posted four catches for 62 yards.

The Ohio State product had one catch for 27 yards in Monday's game before the injury.

Washington will have to figure out a way to replace McLaurin's production by committee. Veteran Stefon Diggs figures to see more targets, while the combination of Dyami Brown, Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams will likely see more playing time.

Brown, Burks and Williams are all potential young building blocks who could be important playmakers both the rest of this season and into the future.

For now, though, the Commanders will have to adjust on the fly without one of their leaders.

articles.title: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin out for the season after suffering knee injury in loss to 49ers
articles.summary: Terry McLaurin's left knee gave out on him as he was running a route on Monday night, and he was carted off the field.
articles.body:
McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon in the Washington Commanders' 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night , head coach Dan Quinn announced. As a result, he will miss the rest of the season.

"I had a chance to speak to him last night on the plane, and again after testing today," Quinn said. "I'm gutted for him."

McLaurin was running a route near the end of the first quarter of Monday's matchup at Levi's Stadium when he suddenly fell near the sideline. Replay showed that McLaurin's left knee gave out on him and buckled as he was planting to the outside.

He remained down on the field for quite some time in front of the Commanders' bench, clearly in pain. A cart eventually came out for him. He hopped up into the back of the vehicle under his own power with his entire left leg in a full air cast, and players from both teams saw him off.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury, and Quinn said after the game that they feared the injury was significant. Now, after an MRI on Tuesday, McLaurin will have to undergo season-ending surgery.

McLaurin had one catch for 27 yards before he went down on Monday night. He'll finish the season, his eighth in the league with the Commanders, with 230 receiving yards and one touchdown.

The injury comes at a tough time for the Commanders. They fell to 1-4-1 on the season after Monday's loss in Santa Clara, which has them last in the NFC East. Though the division is still wide open — remarkably, nobody from the division has won a game in the past two weeks — losing a target like McLaurin is going to make things much more difficult for quarterback Jayden Daniels the rest of the way.

The Commanders are off in Week 7, and will return to take on the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 1.

articles.title: Impactante actualización sobre el caso de OJ Simpson: pudo contar con un cómplice de la mafia en la escena del crimen
articles.standfirst: Un narcotraficante vinculado a la mafia que era confidente del FBI habría aportado información que la fiscalía prefirió no utilizar durante el juicio penal
articles.summary: Un narcotraficante vinculado a la mafia que era confidente del FBI habría aportado información que la fiscalía prefirió no utilizar durante el juicio penal
articles.body: El 12 de junio de 1994 la policía halló los cuerpos sin vida de Nicole Brown y el amigo de esta, Ron Goldman, en una casa de Los Ángeles. Ambas víctimas fueron apuñaladas hasta la muerte mientras estaban en la casa de Brown, exesposa de OJ Simpson. Por aquel entonces, OJ era uno de los rostros más conocidos de Estados Unidos. Tras una brillante carrera en la NFL, el antiguo running back de los Buffalo Bills se desempeñaba como comentarista y actor ocasional; era un tipo carismático y famoso. Simpson fue absuelto de los asesinatos en 1995 tras un juicio penal, pero fue declarado culpable de las muertes en un juicio civil celebrado en 1997. OJ murió en 2024 a los 76 años a causa de un cáncer de próstata. Ahora, 30 años después del proceso judicial, se han desclasificado todos los documentos relacionados con el caso, a los que ha tenido acceso The New York Times, que en un artículo ha desvelado que Simpson pudo contar con un cómplice en la escena del crimen, el cual se habría encargado de deshacerse del arma del crimen. En su momento, la fiscalía sostuvo que OJ actuó solo y nunca pudo presentar el arma homicida, prueba que habría sido esencial y que permitió a la defensa establecer una duda razonable en el jurado. Si bien el caso del asesinato de Nicole Brown y Ron Goldman ha sido desde su inicio objeto de especulaciones, lo que sí sabemos a través de los documentos desclasificados es que un narcotraficante condenado, con vínculos con la mafia y fallecido en 2006, proporcionó al FBI información sobre los citados asesinatos. En concreto, en los documentos se cita que el FBI compartió con la fiscalía información recibida de Joseph ‘Joey’ Ippolito, quien en 1994 -un mes antes de cometerse los crímenes- se fugó de una prisión federal en Florida y se trasladó al sur de California. De hecho, se reconoce a Ippolito como amigo íntimo de Al Cowlings, quien a su vez era una de las personas más cercanas a Simpson. ‘Joey’, a quien el FBI consideraba un "informante fiable", proporcionó a los federales datos sobre actividades mafiosas y también sobre los mencionados asesinatos. Un año después de su fuga, regresaría a prisión. Los lazos entre Cowlings e Ippolito se hicieron evidentes cuando la policía encontró una foto de la novia de este último, justo en el vehículo en el que Simpson protagonizó su famosa fuga televisada con Cowlings al volante. La información proporcionada por ‘Joey’ Ippolito fue puesta en conocimiento de la fiscalía que llevaba el caso de Simpson durante el tramo final del proceso penal, pero estos consideraron que no debía ser compartida con el jurado ni tampoco llamaron a Ippolito a declarar. Los documentos aparecidos sólo citan que Joseph Ippolito proporcionó cierta información sobre ese caso a través del FBI, pero sin ofrecer los detalles. Aquí es donde entra el New York Times, que tras acceder a dichos documentos, entrevistó a Sam Ippolito, uno de los hermanos de ‘Joey’. Este declaró inicialmente que se deshizo de una bolsa que contenía un objeto grande y la ropa ensangrentada de Joseph. Dice que aquella noche de los asesinatos su hermano salió de casa a “ayudar a un amigo” tras hablar con Al Cowlings. Según relata, horas después ‘Joey’ regresó con lo que parecía sangre en las manos y una bolsa que contenía un objeto pesado que le entregó para que se deshiciera de ella, y que tiró al contenedor de una obra cercana. Sin embargo, después de contar todo esto al NYT, Sam Ippolito reclamó dinero a este periódico y, al negarse el periodista que realizó la entrevista, dijo que se retractaba de todo lo dicho.

images.caption: OJ Simpson se intenta poner el guante encontrado en la escena del crimen durante el juicio penal. Lee Celano/WireImage

articles.title: NFL Exec Says League Is Eyeing 10 International Games in 2027, Teases New Cities on Schedule
articles.summary: The NFL is hoping to continue its expansion of the international schedule next season.
articles.body:
The NFL is hoping to continue its expansion of the international schedule next season.

Per Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer, Peter O'Reilly, the league's executive vice president of club business and international and league events, said the NFL is considering adding an additional international game to the 2027 slate after having nine games outside of the United States this year.

In May, NFL owners voted to increase the cap on international games from eight to 10, starting in 2027. That number doesn't factor in the Jacksonville Jaguars' game at Wembley Stadium, so there could be up to 11 international games next year.

After owners approved an additional international game, O'Reilly noted that the league was eyeing a regular-season game in Japan, which would be a first for the NFL. Tokyo previously hosted a preseason game.

This season, the NFL held its first game in Australia as the San Francisco 49ers defeated the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne. France will host an NFL game for the first time on Sunday when the Pittsburgh Steelers take on the New Orleans Saints in Paris.

While the NFL will add another game in 2027, it isn't looking to stop there. NFL commissioner Rodger Goodell said in July that he is hoping to have an international game almost every week, adding that he has "about 10" international markets that he's eyeing.

"We have our eyes set on being 16 games internationally every year," he said. "We think we can do it."

But having so many games outside of the United States isn't a decision Goodell can make without the approval of the NFL Players Association. Whether the NFLPA is willing to take on the additional travel that comes with playing international games remains to be seen.

Goodell's push to add international games is perhaps a part of a bigger plan. He said in August that he has "no doubt" that there will be an NFL team outside the United States "at some point." He's also hoping to have an international city host the Super Bowl.

"There are definitely international cities that could host something like that," he said. "But we would like to see an NFL team in such a city first."

articles.title: Drake Maye battles crippling milkshake addiction, Great White goes airborne and better halftime show ideas
articles.summary: Drake Maye reveals he drank up to three milkshakes a day, while a viral great white shark video and hockey goalie Devin Cooley steal the show.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news, and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. I don't know about you, but I've got that Tuesday feeling, and it's time to dig into some Nightcaps because we've got everything from Drake Maye's obscene milkshake habit to an Air Jaws sighting to discuss. I'm deputizing for the great Amber Harding, and it's good to get back in the saddle after I had a short week last week to celebrate the wife's birthday. And she did it right: an Airbnb with a pool, theater, and game room that was only about 20 minutes from our regular abode, and she invited friends and family over. Between floating in the pool and watching hockey games on the outside TV (which was slightly broken; can't win them all) and watching the Vincent Price vehicle "The Tingler" in the theater, I had to ask myself a couple of times if it was my birthday too. A great time was had by all, but those Airbnbs aren't cheap, and that's why it's back to work for this hombre! So, let's dig right in. Drake Maye had a wild milkshake habit I'm a big milkshake guy, but I like an everyman's milkshake. PATRIOTS' DRAKE MAYE 'LOOKING MYSELF IN THE MIRROR' AS GAME HAS COMPLETELY COLLAPSED SINCE AFC CHAMPIONSHIP All I want is a nice, frosty chocolate shake that is thick, but not so thick that nothing comes through the straw and you pass out. I don't need whipped cream, wacky flavors, or half of a cherry pie sticking out and chocolate syrup squirted all over the top of the glass. Just. A. Milkshake. And I bet Drake Maye has similarly strong opinions because he had a bona fide milkshake problem. In an interview with Men's Health, the Patriots QB revealed that he is trying to cut back from as many as three shakes in a day. SHARK WEEK SHOCKER AS GREAT WHITE BREACHES JUST YARDS FROM OBLIVIOUS BOOGIE BOARDER And no, not protein shakes. The fact that he was crushing that many milkshakes and is a starting quarterback in the NFL is crazy. You'd think he'd be washing himself with a rag on a stick and having to get weighed at the zoo. Unreal. This needs to be studied by science. Smart to cut back, but I bet he takes the occasional late-night trip down to Steak 'N' Shake to whet his whistle when he's jonesing. He's only human. Just when you thought it was okay to go back in the water, some shark goes and does this. I'm not a beach guy. That's partially because of "Jaws" and also because I don't like sand or when seaweed touches my foot. However, I've warmed up to the beach as I've gotten older, but consider me out again after seeing this video of a Great White doing its best Shamu impression off the coast of California that went viral. Now, I'm a veteran "Shark Week" watcher, so I was familiar with the phenomenon of sharks breaching and doing flips like it's the X-Games. I was, however, under the impression that this was something that only happened off the coast of South Africa, which was fine by me. Now, the cartilaginous acrobatics are hitting American shores (technically, they're still off of them, but you know what I mean). This sort of thing never happens in pools... right? NHL goalie goes viral for the goalie-est interviews of all time Perhaps more so than any other position in sports, being a hockey goalie attracts a certain offbeat breed. It makes sense. Most of us would decline if asked to put a huge chunk of the team's fate on our shoulders while fighting off 100 mph howitzers. That's how you wind up with Ilya Bryzgalov talking about the "hu-mang-ous big" universe, or Gilles "Gratoony the Loony" Gratton believing he's a reincarnated conquistador and sitting out a game because the moon was in the wrong part of the sky. Let's add Calgary Flames netminder Devin Cooley to this list. It's been a slow start to the season, but Cooley played well in their recent win over the Carolina Hurricanes, and followed it up with some stellar interviews off of it. I mean, that felt more like a psych lecture than the usual "We just need to go out and get pucks deep" brand of hockey interview, and I'm all about it. There's more where that came from, and apparently, Cooley's teammates all run to the TV when he does an interview, and I think you can see why. Great stuff. Hockey needs more of this. Here are some ideas for acts Jay Z could've hired over himself It sounds like Jay Z has hired himself for the Super Bowl halftime show. I've not been a fan of his work with the Super Bowl halftime show over the last few years. Save for the one with Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, and Dr. Dre, most have been forgettable as far as the production is concerned. I mean, can anyone remember any specific moments from them since he started in 2019? Not really. There hasn't been any Prince guitar solo, Bob Ross-looking slackline guy, or Janet Jackson nipple to speak of. Nonetheless, I like some of his tunes, and I kind of respect the audacity to be like, "Alright, the best person to do this is... me." I wish I had more of that. Still, it wouldn't be a Super Bowl halftime show if we didn't go over some acts that would've been great to see instead. Metallica -Whenever the idea of a rock band doing Super Bowl halftime show duties comes up, 'Tallica is always first. They like big, unusual gigs. That's why they played in Antarctica and are currently in the midst of a Sphere residency. Speaking of which, have you seen what they do when they play "The Call of Ktulu" there? Bring that level of show to the Super Bowl. Foo Fighters - If Metallica is busy, the next number most people call when they need a rock and/or metal band is Dave Grohl and Co., and I think they could do it. They've got plenty of hits and bring the energy as well as any band out there. Trying not to sing along with "Monkey Wrench." You can't. Jack White - Now, I know he's got a sprinkling of TDS, but the man's repertoire speaks for itself. Plus, he played the Thanksgiving halftime show in Detroit just last year to rave reviews. Maybe he brings Meg White out for "Seven Nation Army" or something. It would be awesome. The Muppets - Everyone would love this, and if you want to see 65,000 people weeping, just let Kermit the Frog whip out his banjo and uncork a stirring rendition of "Rainbow Connection." Any country artist - I looked it up, and there have been some sporadic country artists over the years, like Shania Twain in 2003, and a full-fledged country-fied halftime show in the mid-1990s. But as big as country music has gotten, how has this not happened again? There are plenty who could handle it. Hell, Ella Langley has been annihilating the Billboard charts lately. Trot Chris Stapleton out there for a few songs with special guests, and I can assure you, there will be no complaints. Still, best of luck to Jay Z, and what are the odds we get a Kanye cameo? I'm going to guess quite low. Yay or Nay on a possible all-indoor World Series? I'm really looking forward to the World Series, because I'm psyched to see a new franchise win a World Series, but I'm torn on one aspect of it. The indoors-ed-ness. This has the potential to be the first completely indoor World Series ever. Obviously, Tropicana Field is indoors, while American Family Field has a roof that can be opened and closed. This is great for getting the series played on time... but it still feels wrong. I don't like this trend we're seeing with more and more teams moving inside. Sure, I get the logistics and the financial upsides, but who doesn't get excited to see a football game in snow or a World Series game where you can see the players' breath. I'll tell you: no one. I hope the folks in Milwaukee come to their senses and pop the roof open if the weather is clear but cold. Give the people what they want, and maybe a little icing on that slide will help Bernie get a little extra speed. ... CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That's it for this edition of Nightcaps! See you tomorrow!

After being released by Tampa Bay ahead of the 2025 season, Trask joined the Atlanta Falcons' practice squad for the end of the campaign. He signed with the Carolina Panthers during training camp but was released during final roster cuts.

While Trask won't be a part of the Cowboys' active roster, he's likely an injury away from being promoted since Prescott and Sam Howell are the only two quarterbacks on the team at the moment.

articles.title: Brandon McManus, Rams Agree to Contract as New Kicker After Blake Grupe's Season-Ending injury
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams signed veteran kicker Brandon McManus on Tuesday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams signed veteran kicker Brandon McManus on Tuesday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo .

McManus and free-agent kicker Matt Prater worked out for Los Angeles earlier on Tuesday, per Rapoport and Garafolo.

The Rams were in need of a new kicker after Blake Grupe suffered a season-ending torn ACL during their 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

Grupe's injury occurred while attempting to make a tackle in the first quarter of the contest.

Los Angeles opened the 2026 season with second-year kicker Harrison Mevis as its starter, but cut ties with him following a string of inconsistent performances.

Mevis connected on just 55.6 percent of his field goals through five games, going 3-for-7 from at least 40 yards away.

After he missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and had a 48-yarder blocked in the Rams' overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5, he was released.

As for McManus, he's played for three teams across his 12 years in the NFL and has 186 games under his belt.

The 35-year-old spent the 2025 season with the Green Bay Packers, connecting on 80.0 percent of his field goals. He hit three of his five attempts from at least 50 yards out.

The Rams will hope that McManus can bring some more stability to their special teams unit and help them bounce back from a disappointing 2-4 start to their 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Amid civil unrest in Paris, NFL has 'never been close' to moving first game in France
articles.summary: NFL officials have been in Paris for about 10 days working on logistics, league exec Peter O'Reilly said. "We've got confidence in the plans, both from an op...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — The NFL's first game in France is scheduled for Sunday between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints.

The game is expected to continue as scheduled despite unrest in Paris and across France. About 2,400 people were arrested nationwide over the weekend amid riots over living costs and poor conditions in schools, per the Associated Press .

"All of our plans for the Paris game this weekend are moving forward as planned," said Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president of club business, international and league events, on Tuesday from league meetings. "We're obviously working and collaborating very closely with the Parisian French authorities, as well as the State Department. Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams. …

"We've got confidence in the plans, both from an ops and a security standpoint."

NFL officials have been in Paris for about 10 days working on logistics, O'Reilly said. Among those on the ground is NFL senior vice president of security Cathy Lanier, who previously served as the Chief of Police for the Washington D.C. Metropolitan Police Department.

Stade de France, where the game will be staged, has hosted major international games before, including the 2024 Paris Olympics.

The Saints flew from New York to Paris on Sunday night after beating the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. The Steelers are scheduled to fly to Paris on Thursday.

"All of our events we have going on, we always have a very strong security presence around all of those events," O'Reilly said. "And that presence will be heightened with local authorities making sure that there's nothing more important from our standpoint than the team security, the fan security, everybody involved with this game. So, extremely vigilant, as we always are. As I said, confident in all of those plans as we head towards Sunday."

The NFL has previously considered relocating domestic games when natural disasters, such as wildfires in Southern California, have dictated that resources not be redirected to a football game. O'Reilly said that is not a concern for the league with the game and surrounding fan events.

"We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," O'Reilly said. "That's always top of mind for us and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."

The Saints improved to 2-4 with their 34-27 win over the Giants. The Steelers arrive at 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

France marks the third new market this season for the NFL, which played in Melbourne, Australia and Rio de Janeiro, Brazil this fall after two seasons playing in São Paolo. The NFL has nine total international games this season across Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro, London, Paris, Madrid, Munich and Mexico City.

O'Reilly said the league is considering expanding to 10 international games next year, which is the maximum amount allowed by the league's current collective bargaining agreement with the NFL Players Association.

The NFL continues to have interest in playing a game in Asia, and particularly Japan, but has not finalized plans to announce a game there yet. Some countries that hosted games this year are likely to win bids for 2027, including some games in new cities for returning countries akin to the NFL's recent model in Brazil.

Has the NFL considered moving the game out of Paris due to unrest?

"We have never been close to that point," O'Reilly said. "We've always got contingency plans for every game, every single one of them. But no, we were not at that point at any point in the conversation."

articles.title: Eagles' Hollywood Brown 'Could Be Traded' Ahead of Deadline, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Hollywood Brown's time in Philadelphia could be fairly short-lived.
articles.body:
Hollywood Brown's time in Philadelphia could be fairly short-lived.

According to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the Eagles could look to move the veteran wideout—who was inactive for the past four games—in a trade:

Report: Eagles Won't Be Punished for Hurts

Brown, 29, has not appeared in a game for the Eagles since Week 2, dealing with an ankle injury after that (though he was a healthy inactive on Sunday). While he was never expected to crack the top trio of DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks or rookie Makai Lemon, there was a thought that perhaps he could have a role in certain packages.

Instead, it was players like Darius Cooper trusted with a bigger role when Smith was hurt, while Elijah Moore appears to have secured the WR5 spot on the depth chart (and Britain Covey is also on the roster, albeit primarily as a special-teams player). Brown hasn't registered a reception and has two carries for 12 yards.

He appeared to be headed to stardom after registering 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six touchdowns with the Baltimore Ravens in 2021, his third NFL season. But Brown's breakout campaign was followed by a number of injuries and diminishing returns in stints with the Arizona Cardinals (2022-23) and Kansas City Chiefs (2024-25).

He did manage 49 catches for 587 yards and five scores in 2025.

Whether the Eagles are actively shopping him or his agent is simply trying to drum up interest is unclear. But there's likely a muted market for a player unable to crack Philadelphia's wideout rotation.

articles.title: NFL VP says league is 'vigilant' about security for France matchup, remains confident in plans

articles.title: Ryan Miller Lands Patriots Role After Miami Cut
articles.summary: The Patriots signed receiver Ryan Miller to their practice squad following Romeo Doubs hitting IR. Miller brings explosive 77-yard touchdown potential to New...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots found a hidden gem in the Miami Dolphins' recent roster cuts. According to the NFL's official transaction log, the team added wide receiver Ryan Miller to the practice squad on Monday.

This move solves an immediate problem for New England. The team had to place Romeo Doubs on injured reserve after a shoulder injury during the 26-19 win over the New York Jets on Sunday. Losing Doubs leaves a gap in the receiving corps that Miller might fill.

Explosive potential in the practice squad

Miller isn't just a depth piece; he has shown he can score big. During his time with Miami, he caught a 77-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Malik Willis against the San Francisco 49ers on September 20, per Heavy.com . That single play accounted for a huge chunk of his production. He finished his five games with Miami with three catches for 92 yards and one touchdown.

He brings more than just one big play to the building. Before his time in Miami, Miller played three seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In 11 games during the 2024 season, he tallied 12 catches, 128 yards, and two touchdowns. He also had a productive 2025 season with two catches for 34 yards and a touchdown.

Miller's journey to the NFL was not a standard one. He played his college football at Furman, a school better known for basketball. The Patriots' official announcement states he has played in 30 career games, starting six of them.

Former Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles once praised the receiver's skill set. The Buccaneers' official website quoted Bowles as saying, "Ryan is smart, he's reliable, he's tough."

The Patriots now have a veteran presence on the practice squad. While players like A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III are active, Miller provides essential cover. He enters a group that already includes practice squad players Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner, and Chandler Brayboy.

articles.title: Steelers Power Rankings Roundup: Where Pittsburgh Landed After Week 6
articles.summary: Pittsburgh improved to 4-2 with an overtime win over Tampa Bay, but not every outlet was sold. Here's where six major publications ranked the Steelers.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a comeback win, but their latest NFL power rankings show there is still work to do.

Pittsburgh rallied from a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime, improving to 4-2 on the season. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard delivered a breakout performance, while Jaylen Warren continued to establish himself as the Steelers' lead running back.

The win helped Pittsburgh move up in several rankings, though some outlets remain concerned about the team's offensive consistency heading into Week 7.

Pittsburgh moved up three spots in ESPN's NFL power rankings , going from No. 20 to No. 17.

The outlet pointed to third-down efficiency as the Steelers' biggest offensive issue. Pittsburgh has converted just 33% of its third-down attempts this season, ranking among the five worst teams in the NFL.

Pittsburgh stayed at No. 16 in The Athletic's power rankings , with the focus on the changing picture in the Steelers' backfield.

Jaylen Warren has emerged as Pittsburgh's top running back, pushing Rico Dowdle down the fantasy rankings. Dowdle was drafted 73rd on average but sits at No. 215 in fantasy scoring, while Warren ranks 42nd overall and leads all Steelers.

Pittsburgh made a four-spot jump in The Sporting News' power rankings , rising from No. 14 to No. 10.

The Steelers' passing game received attention despite Rodgers taking five sacks against Tampa Bay. He threw multiple touchdown passes for the fourth consecutive game, continuing a productive stretch for Pittsburgh's offense.

Bleacher Report dropped Pittsburgh one spot, from No. 14 to No. 15, despite its overtime win.

The outlet highlighted Bernard's performance against Tampa Bay. He finished with 11 catches for 83 yards and a touchdown after entering the game with only 13 receptions on the season.

Pittsburgh's ability to work through adversity also factored into the assessment. The Steelers have won three of their last four games, and Bleacher Report pointed to the team's experience as an advantage as it continues to find its footing.

Pittsburgh slipped from a three-way tie at No. 12 to stand-alone No. 13 in Pro Football Talk's rankings .

The outlet offered a brief, cryptic assessment of the Steelers, writing, "Time to get Le Torchon Terrible ready." The ranking placed Pittsburgh in the upper half of the league despite the slight drop.

USA Today moved the Steelers down one spot, from No. 17 to No. 18.

Bernard was again the focus. Through his first two starts, the rookie has recorded 17 receptions and now has 24 catches on the season, the second-most among all rookies.

His performance against Tampa Bay gave Pittsburgh another encouraging development on offense, particularly as the Steelers look for more consistency in the passing game.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Announce Two Roster Moves Ahead of Packers Showdown
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have signed Aidan Keanaaina to their practice squad and released Chris Smith ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions made two roster moves Tuesday as they continue preparing for Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Green Bay Packers. And one of those moves brings a familiar defensive lineman back to Detroit after an injury disrupted his rookie season.

The Lions officially announced that they have signed defensive tackle Aidan Keanaaina to the practice squad and released defensive lineman Chris Smith to make room. The move comes just one day after Keanaaina reportedly visited the organization.

Detroit Lions Bring Back Aidan Keanaaina

Keanaaina originally signed with Detroit as an undrafted free agent following the 2026 NFL Draft after playing college football at Notre Dame and California. The 6-foot-3, 320-pound defensive tackle showed enough promise to earn an opportunity with the Lions before suffering an injury during training camp.

Detroit placed Keanaaina on injured reserve in August before eventually reaching an injury settlement with the rookie. With that settlement period behind him, the Lions have now decided to bring him back into the organization.

As we reported Monday , Keanaaina recently visited the Lions as the team evaluated potential defensive-line additions. Tuesday's official announcement confirms Detroit has decided to move forward with the reunion.

During his final college season at California, Keanaaina recorded 56 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks. His size and experience defending the interior make him an intriguing developmental option for a Lions team looking to maintain depth along its defensive front.

Chris Smith Released From Lions Practice Squad

To create room for Keanaaina, Detroit released Chris Smith, who had been part of the organization's defensive-line depth for multiple seasons. Smith joined the Lions after going undrafted out of Notre Dame in 2023 and appeared in five regular-season games for Detroit in 2024.

Smith had spent the first six weeks of the 2026 season on Detroit's practice squad without receiving a game-day elevation. Despite earning praise from Dan Campbell for his work ethic and attention to detail, the Lions have decided to move in another direction.

The decision also continues Detroit's efforts to develop younger defensive linemen behind its established contributors. As we previously reported , the Lions recently added Jeffrey M'Ba to their practice squad, providing another developmental option along the defensive interior.

According to the Tuesday transaction report , Keanaaina received a substantial guaranteed commitment from Detroit when he initially signed as an undrafted rookie. The Lions' decision to bring him back suggests the organization remains interested in evaluating his long-term potential.

The team's earlier official roster transactions also document Keanaaina's original signing and subsequent placement on injured reserve. His return to the practice squad does not mean he has been added to the active roster for Sunday's matchup.

For now, the Lions have swapped one defensive tackle for another on the practice squad. But after bringing Keanaaina back into the building, Brad Holmes and Detroit's coaching staff will get another opportunity to develop a young player they originally targeted following the draft.

articles.title: 49ers owner Jed York makes first public appearance since arrest
articles.summary: York attended the NFL owners meeting on the day his suspension officially ended.
articles.body:
Clearly, San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was ready for his NFL suspension to end and wasted no time before reemerging in the public eye.

Nearly two months after York was arrested in a prostitution sting operation on Aug. 23 near his Ohio hometown, York made his first public appearance at the NFL owners meeting on Tuesday in New York. USA Today reporter Chris Bumbaca posted a video showing York walking through the lobby and heading to the first day of the NFL's two days of meetings in Manhattan.

The appearance comes eight weeks and one day after York's arrest first became public knowledge, with York pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges in court on Aug. 24. York was ordered to pay $1,150 in fines and sentenced to serve one day in jail for each charge, which were served concurrently.

York skipped the last one-day owners meeting, which took place in Atlanta on Aug. 26 - just three days after his arrest. 49ers CEO Al Guido attended in York's place for the meeting, which was mainly held to approve the sale of the Seahawks to the Khosla family.

York's eagerness to return to work and get out from under the cloud of his arrest and suspension is not exactly a shock. He willingly kept himself away from the team for the first three weeks of the NFL season, even though the league hadn't officially suspended him yet. The NFL then gave him credit for those missed games in announcing his suspension on Oct. 2 , shortening his punishment. (Left unexplained in all of this is an ESPN report that York still traveled all the way to Melbourne, Australia, ahead of the 49ers' Week 1 game in the city against the Rams, even though York did not attend the game.)

According to San Francisco Standard columnist Tim Kawakami, York was expected to "immediately be back in charge--publicly and privately--as soon as his suspension ended." Kawakami also believes that York's attendance at Tuesday's meeting means he'll be in Atlanta on Sunday, when the Niners face the Falcons.

York did not answer questions from media members on Tuesday prior to the meetings starting and has not talked to the media at all since his arrest, only offering a single public comment via a statement when the NFL announced his suspension.

Hurts’ treatment involves blood thinners, and he will not be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is off them. articles.title: Dan Quinn Calls Out Jayden Daniels for 4th-Down Mistake, QB Responds After Commanders Loss to 49ers
articles.summary: Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn wasn't a fan of quarterback Jayden Daniels' fourth-down decision in the first half of a 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn wasn't a fan of quarterback Jayden Daniels' fourth-down decision in the first half of a 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night.

"Even when you know there's a penalty, you still take your shot, man, to go throw it, complete it," Quinn said, per ESPN's John Keim . "You don't know if it's gonna get picked up."

With Washington trailing 13-3 and the ball at San Francisco's 13-yard line in the second quarter, the Commanders chose to go for it on fourth down and two yards to gain. Daniels took the snap and launched a pass out of the back of the end zone as a flag was thrown, although the penalty was on Washington.

"I didn't know. It could have been offside, it could have been on us," Daniels said when asked if he anticipated an offside call on the 49ers, per Keim.

There was some buzz surrounding Quinn potentially being confused about what down it was, although he said that wasn't the case.

"Definitely knew it was fourth down," Quinn told reporters after the game. "We were going for it... We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game. I didn't think it was going to be a 17-14 game; I thought it was probably gonna be a 28-30 game."

The Commanders were still able to pull within one score in the fourth quarter of the contest, but turned the ball over on downs with two minutes left before Daniels was sacked while attempting a game-winning touchdown pass as time expired.

Daniels finished 29-of-40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns without tossing an interception. He also rushed for 10 yards.

With the defeat, Washington fell to 1-4-1.

articles.title: What to know about Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts' agent and the Eagles said in a statement Monday his "prognosis is very good, and we anticipate a full recovery."
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, a Super Bowl champion and one of the NFL's top stars, is now facing a long absence because of blood clots in his lungs — and his team is facing serious questions over his medical treatment.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles said in a statement Monday his "prognosis is very good, and we anticipate a full recovery."

The condition can be life-threatening, and the Eagles say Hurts could miss the rest of the season.

However, Hurts was cleared to play a week ago in London after a blood clot was found in his leg. He threw for 222 yards and a touchdown, but the Eagles lost to the Jacksonville Jaguars, 19-17.

Just one day earlier, he was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his left calf and ordered by doctors to stay awake overnight, according to NFL insiders, who report the quarterback did not sleep for roughly 36 hours. After being released from the hospital, he was reportedly given some time to rest before taking the field against the Jaguars.

The NFL in a statement Tuesday disputed that reporting, calling it "misinformation" that Hurts did not sleep for 36 hours before the Oct. 11 game.

"That was not true and no one told him not to sleep because of his situation," NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said. "The club told all players, coaches and personnel to try to stay awake as long as they could on Saturday as the team was returning back home after the game in London. The team did not have a bye week and like other NFL teams that travel to London and back, they were trying maintain as much of a normal routine as possible."

Since then, the diagnosis has worsened. The star quarterback is now facing deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli with blood clots in his left leg and both lungs, the team and his agent said.

Deep vein thrombosis, also known as DVT, refers to a condition when a blood clot develops in the deep veins, usually in the lower extremities, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . A pulmonary embolism, or PE, is the term for when the clot breaks off and travels to the lungs, which can be life-threatening, the CDC says.

"You have a clot in your leg. The problem is it can travel up the veins and go to your heart, and from there, go to your lungs, and block the blood vessels in your lungs. And you get things called pulmonary emboli. That's very serious," CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook, who is not treating Hurts, told "CBS Mornings."

Whether it could be career-ending, LaPook said, it's "too soon to know."

"Normally what you do is you would treat this with blood thinners for three months and then sort of see what happens," he continued. "Now, they're going to follow him closely. It may be more than that, and then after that, you take them off the blood thinners."

LaPook said Hurts' doctors would then likely test his blood to see if there is an issue that increases the risk of clotting.

The revelation of the diagnosis is sparking backlash against the Eagles and its medical staff.

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not answer Monday why the quarterback was allowed to play in London or fly back with the team to the U.S. after the game.

"I'm not a medical expert. I lean on our guys in all those situations, right? I'm a football coach," he said. "I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them."

McCarthy in his statement Tuesday said that the NFL has "been in contact throughout the process with the Eagles medical personnel, and the Cleveland Clinic in London where the tests were conducted."

The National Football League Players Association, the union which represents the players, is demanding the league conduct a "full investigation into what occurred."

An NFLPA spokesperson told CBS News in a statement Tuesday night that it was "not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," adding that the league had "previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received."

A main question from fans is whether flying to London, or flying back, could have exacerbated the injury. LaPook said it's possible it could be an issue.

"In flying, you can get dehydrated, you're not moving around a lot," so your blood doesn't return to your heart as well, LaPook said. "When he got there (to London), they did a test, and they found this superficial thrombophlebitis, so a little clot, and they ... clear him to play. He ended up playing, and then right after the game, he flew back."

The fact Hurts did not sleep much was not as big a concern as the flying, LaPook said.

"Well, the bigger point to me is not the not sleeping, it's the fact that he had a flight there, a flight back within a few days," he said. "That increases the risk of blood clot in the first place. We tell people when they're on flights to walk around, maybe wear compression stockings."

The CDC makes similar warnings about flying.

"Extended periods of limited mobility are inherent to long-distance travel and can increase a traveler's risk for VTE," according to the agency. "An association between VTE and air travel was first reported in the early 1950s; since then, long-distance air travel has become more common, leading to increased concerns about travel-associated VTE."

Different organizations offer different guidance on how soon someone with DVT should fly, but they are significantly longer than the time it took for Hurts to fly back to the U.S.

The International Air Transport Association says if a person is stable, they should wait at least five days before a flight, while the British Thoracic Society advises someone with DVT or PE should wait two weeks before flying.

"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts," the Eagles and Hurts' agent said in the statement announcing his long-term absence.

For now, the Eagles will wait three months to see how the condition is improving with blood thinners.

"We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners," the statement said. "In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."
